blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — trastuzumab cardiotoxicity and LVEF monitoring
stem: A client is beginning intravenous trastuzumab (HERCEPTIN) as adjuvant therapy. Which cardiac-monitoring plan is consistent with the current prescribing information?

options.A: Measure LVEF immediately before treatment, every 3 months during therapy and at completion, then every 6 months for at least 2 years after completion of adjuvant therapy.
options.B: Measure LVEF only after symptoms of heart failure appear, because routine baseline and serial assessments are not recommended for asymptomatic clients receiving trastuzumab.
options.C: Measure LVEF once when the adjuvant course is completed, then repeat annually; a pretreatment LVEF and measurements during active therapy are unnecessary.
options.D: Use routine complete blood counts as the primary surveillance for trastuzumab cardiomyopathy and reserve echocardiography or MUGA assessment for severe hematologic abnormalities.

rationale: Current HERCEPTIN labeling warns that trastuzumab can cause cardiomyopathy and asymptomatic decreases in left ventricular ejection fraction. The recommended cardiac-monitoring schedule is a baseline LVEF immediately before treatment, LVEF every 3 months during treatment and upon completion, repeat LVEF every 4 weeks if HERCEPTIN is withheld for significant left ventricular dysfunction, and—when HERCEPTIN is used as adjuvant therapy—LVEF every 6 months for at least 2 years after completion. Therefore A is correct for this adjuvant-therapy stem. B delays monitoring until symptoms, C omits required baseline and treatment-period surveillance, and D substitutes a laboratory test that does not assess ventricular function.
educational_objective: Apply the labeled trastuzumab cardiac-monitoring schedule: obtain baseline LVEF, reassess every 3 months during therapy and at completion, and for adjuvant therapy continue LVEF monitoring every 6 months for at least 2 years after completion.
source_organization: DailyMed (U.S. National Library of Medicine) / FDA labeling

source_claim_supported: HERCEPTIN can cause cardiomyopathy and decreased LVEF; recommended monitoring includes baseline LVEF, every 3 months during and at completion, and for adjuvant therapy every 6 months for at least 2 years after completion.

candidate_reasons_resolved: Rewrote all four choices as complete cardiac-monitoring plans without the original absolute-word distractor cue.
Specified adjuvant therapy in the stem so the post-treatment every-6-month-for-at-least-2-years recommendation is directly applicable, and balanced option length.
audit_note: Independent adversarial review confirms A uniquely reproduces the current HERCEPTIN cardiac-monitoring schedule for adjuvant therapy. B delays surveillance, C omits baseline/serial monitoring, and D uses an unrelated test; no second defensible answer remains.
